pca-exam-overview-diagram-1.caption: Section weightings from the exam guide. Designing and planning carries the most weight; the three sections at the bottom together are 40 percent.
notes: 1. 1. Designing and planning a cloud solution architecture (~25%): Business and technical requirements; network, storage and compute; migration; future improvements.
2. 2. Managing and provisioning infrastructure (~17.5%): Network topologies, storage, compute, Agent Platform ML workflows, prebuilt APIs.
3. 3. Designing for security and compliance (~17.5%): IAM, hierarchy, data security, VPC Service Controls, supply chain, AI security, regulation.
4. 4. Analyzing and optimizing processes (~15%): SDLC, CI/CD, troubleshooting, DR, stakeholder and change management, cost.
5. 5. Managing implementation (~12.5%): Advising teams, API management (Apigee), SDKs, emulators, Terraform.
6. 6. Ensuring solution and operations excellence (~12.5%): Operational excellence pillar, observability, release management, reliability testing.

business-requirements-wellarchitected-di.caption: Requirements drive design. Each non-functional requirement should become a measurable target that you can design, test and monitor.
notes: 1. Business goal: Revenue, cost, speed, risk
4. Decision + KPIs: ROI, SLO, cost, risk

business-requirements-wellarchitected-di.caption: Pillars of the framework and the question each helps you answer in a design.
notes: 1. Operational excellence: Can we deploy, observe and run it efficiently? Automation, monitoring, incident response, continuous improvement.
2. Security, privacy and compliance: Is data protected and access least-privilege? Defence in depth, zero trust, compliance.
3. Reliability: Does it meet availability and recovery targets? Redundancy, graceful degradation, SLOs, tested recovery.
4. Cost optimization: Do we pay only for needed value? Right-sizing, commitments, lifecycle, FinOps visibility.
5. Performance optimization: Does it scale and respond fast enough? Right service, caching, load testing, autoscaling.
6. Sustainability: Can we reduce environmental impact? Efficient regions, utilization, lifecycle of data.

iam-resource-hierarchy-diagram-1.caption: Evaluation order. Deny policies and organization policy restrict even where an allow exists.
notes: 1. Organization policy constraints: What configurations are allowed at all (for example no external IPs)
2. VPC Service Controls: Which API calls may cross a perimeter
3. IAM deny policies: Explicit denials that override allows
4. IAM allow policies (inherited + conditions): Union of grants from org, folder, project and resource
5. Resource-level controls: Bucket policies, ACLs (if enabled), database users

data-protection-kms-secrets-diagram-1.section: Encryption by default and key options
data-protection-kms-secrets-diagram-1.caption: Increasing key control, moving from the default to keys held outside Google Cloud.
notes: 1. Google-managed encryption (default): No configuration; automatic rotation; no customer key control

2. CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys): Keys in Cloud KMS that you create, rotate, disable and destroy; supported by most services (Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Compute, GKE, Cloud SQL, Spanner, Pub/Sub…)
3. CMEK with Cloud HSM: Keys protected in FIPS 140-2 Level 3 hardware security modules
4. Cloud EKM (external key manager): Keys remain in a supported external key manager outside Google; you can cut off access to data instantly
5. CSEK (customer-supplied keys): You provide the key with each request; only Cloud Storage and Compute Engine disks; you must keep the key or lose the data

perimeter-controls-diagram-1.caption: A perimeter protects services in the production projects. Requests from inside or from allowed access levels succeed; others are denied.
notes: Internet / other project → Cloud Storage: denied (dashed connection)

supply-chain-ai-security-diagram-1.caption: A secured delivery chain. Each stage produces evidence that the next stage checks.
notes: 1. Source: Protected branches, code review, signed commits, Secret scanning
2. Build: Cloud Build, hermetic and isolated; SLSA provenance
3. Store: Artifact Registry, vulnerability scanning, immutable tags
4. Attest: Sign images; attestations after tests and scans
5. Admit: Binary Authorization policy at deploy time

compliance-governance-diagram-1.caption: Layers of compliance control: policy, platform, data, evidence.
notes: 1. Governance: Policies, data owners, DPAs, risk register, training
2. Guardrails: Organization policy, Assured Workloads, hierarchical firewall, VPC Service Controls
3. Data protection: Classification, CMEK/EKM, DLP, retention and residency
4. Identity and access: Least privilege, PAM, MFA, separation of duties
5. Evidence: Audit logs, Asset Inventory, SCC compliance, reports, regular reviews

sdlc-cicd-testing-diagram-1.section: A CI/CD pipeline on Google Cloud
sdlc-cicd-testing-diagram-1.caption: From commit to production. Every stage produces evidence and gates the next.
notes: 1. Source: GitHub, GitLab, Developer Connect, Cloud Source Repositories legacy
2. Build + test: Cloud Build triggers, unit tests, SAST
4. Deploy: Cloud Deploy pipeline: dev → staging → prod
5. Verify + operate: Smoke tests, SLO monitoring, rollback

troubleshooting-dr-testing-diagram-1.caption: Stabilise first, then diagnose, then fix the cause, then learn.
notes: 2. Mitigate: Rollback, failover, scale, disable feature
3. Diagnose: Hypotheses from signals, narrow the scope
4. Fix: Permanent change via normal pipeline

business-processes-finops-diagram-1.caption: Cost optimisation layers, from visibility to commitments.
notes: 1. Visibility and allocation: Billing export to BigQuery, labels, projects/folders, budgets and alerts, Looker Studio dashboards
2. Eliminate waste: Delete idle resources, snapshots, unattached disks; Recommender (idle VMs, over-provisioned); lifecycle policies
3. Right-size and re-architect: Custom machine types, autoscaling, serverless, Autoclass, BigQuery partitioning/clustering
4. Price better: Committed use discounts (resource-based and flexible), sustained use discounts, Spot VMs, BigQuery editions/reservations, enterprise agreements
5. Governance: Quotas, organization policy limits on machine types and regions, showback/chargeback, FinOps culture

case-study-technique-diagram-1.section: A method for any case study
case-study-technique-diagram-1.caption: Extract, map, then answer. Build the requirement list once and reuse it for every question tied to the case.
notes: 1. Business drivers: Why the company is changing; success metrics
2. Existing estate: Current systems, locations, teams, licences
3. Requirements: Technical, security, compliance, cost, timeline
4. Constraints: Skills, contracts, data location, uptime windows
5. Map to services: One line per requirement
6. Answer: Choose the option that satisfies the most stated requirements

exam-technique-and-review-diagram-1.caption: A four-pass reading method. Constraint words decide the answer, not familiar service names.

2. Constraints: Cost, latency, residency, skills, effort, time
3. Eliminate: Cross out options violating a constraint
4. Pick: Most managed option that satisfies all
